video_observation: The body remains approximately level and the legs keep cycling throughout the sampled sequence. The camera follows the robot, so screen position alone cannot measure forward progress.
interpretation: Useful retention case: a reward change should preserve forward tracking and balance. Upright does not mean zero joint oscillation.

video_observation: The robot remains upright but its orientation progressively changes, especially in the latter half. The overlay requests lateral motion with zero yaw rate.
interpretation: Balance and directional tracking must be scored separately. The overlay reaches 0.6 m/s lateral, above the saved training range of ±0.3 m/s; repeat diagnosis within that range.

video_observation: The robot approaches, steps onto the tiles, crosses the patch, and returns to the surrounding flat surface. Posture varies at transitions, but no tip is visible in the reviewed frames.
interpretation: Preserve this capability. Penalizing every rapid movement or impact could remove useful terrain adaptations.

video_observation: The body pitches with the descent and later returns toward level after leaving the ramp. The robot remains supported in the reviewed sequence, with a visible heading change.
interpretation: A body inclination near the terrain slope is not automatically unwanted jitter. Retain successful descent while tracking heading error.

video_observation: Near the ramp entrance the robot rotates and progresses diagonally/across the slope. Around 12–13 seconds of video it descends off the side and continues on surrounding flat ground.
interpretation: This is a lane-exit failure despite survival. An upright-only success test would incorrectly reward this outcome.

video_observation: After reaching the first step, the robot repeatedly changes leg extension and body inclination near the lower steps. Its heading changes, progress remains limited, and the final sequence shows a large rotation into the tip threshold.
interpretation: The task failure includes limited progress, repeated corrections and loss of balance. A smoother action curve alone will not establish successful ascent.

video_observation: The approach reaches the lower step. The body lowers and rotates near the step, followed by rapid loss of upright posture near the end. It does not complete the staircase.
interpretation: Filtering does not rescue this example. It tips sooner after contact than the unfiltered seed-0 reference; shorter failure episodes also complicate whole-run oscillation comparisons.

video_observation: The robot approaches the lower steps, rotates away from its original heading, and travels across/along the lower stair region. By roughly 17–19 seconds of video it moves off onto surrounding flat ground and continues upright.
interpretation: Wider target limits change the failure mode but do not produce valid ascent. Staying upright by leaving the staircase is a failure, not a fix.
